profile.reading:
TierPoint operates a data center at 15707 Chenal Parkway in Little Rock, Arkansas, spanning more than 30,000 total square feet with more than 9,000 square feet of raised floor, backed by two 2.25-megawatt redundant generators providing more than 48 hours of runtime. The facility holds SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II certifications including HITRUST, and is HIPAA, PCI-DSS, GLBA, ISO 27001, and ITAR compliant, TierPoint's standard compliance package across its portfolio. TierPoint, headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri, was formed in 2010 and grew substantially through acquisitions, including a 575 million dollar, all-cash purchase of Windstream Hosted Solutions' data center assets that closed in December 2015. Windstream itself was headquartered in Little Rock at the time, which makes that 2015 acquisition a plausible route by which this specific facility entered TierPoint's portfolio, though TierPoint's own press release announcing the Windstream deal does not name specific facilities or cities, so this entry records that connection as a plausible but unconfirmed hypothesis rather than a sourced fact. No opening year or specific Uptime Institute Tier level is disclosed on TierPoint's own page for this facility, and no independent local news coverage could be located this session because search-tool quota was exhausted. As is standard industry practice, tenant identities are not publicly disclosed. These gaps are recorded honestly rather than filled with unverified detail.

TierPoint has also grown through significant recent capital raises beyond its acquisition history: a 320 million dollar equity round in April 2020 led by Argo Infrastructure Partners, Wafra, and Macquarie Capital Principal Finance alongside existing investors, followed by Argo's 500 million dollar investment in February 2022 that made it TierPoint's largest single equity investor, and a further increase to Argo's ownership and capital commitment announced in December 2025. TierPoint has also completed several asset-backed securitizations in recent years, reflecting continued institutional confidence in the company's data center portfolio as it has expanded across its 20 US markets.

reading.body:
TierPoint Little Rock publishes 9,000 square feet of technical space and no IT load figure in megawatts, making it impossible to assess its relevance to AI infrastructure scaling.

The absence of a power figure is the binding constraint on understanding this facility's role in AI. Without megawatts, there is no path to calculating rack count, accelerator density, or actual compute capacity. The footprint is small by hyperscale standards. This facility cannot be ranked against AI infrastructure by the metric that determines scaling decisions.

The six certifications reveal what workloads this facility is built to host. SOC 1 Type 2 and ISO 27001 establish audited controls over financial systems and information security. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card processing. HIPAA and HITRUST together qualify it for protected health information, with HITRUST adding validated control frameworks beyond the regulatory baseline. ITAR qualifies it for defense-related technical data. None of these certifications addresses the high-density power infrastructure that AI training requires.

Arkansas has two facilities in this registry, neither publishing a megawatt figure. The state total is zero published MW. TierPoint Little Rock ranks first in the state only because no facility here publishes any power data. For readers evaluating whether this campus matters to AI, the data describes a compliance-oriented colocation facility of modest size with no published indicators of AI training or large-scale inference capacity.
